mainTopic: Whether a Jewish court's death sentence makes a man presumed dead, and when an agent bringing a גט may hand it to another agent.
overview: The amud opens by finishing רב יוסף's statement: a man sentenced by a Jewish court is presumed executed, because once the verdict is final, the court does not look for new reasons to acquit. The גמרא tries to prove this from a משנה about a runaway convict, but a runaway may be different. A second proof comes from a ברייתא about death reports, but it is pushed off: gentile officials are not believed because they want their verdict to look carried out. A new משנה teaches that a sick agent may pass a גט to another agent, unless the husband also asked him to collect an item from the wife. רב כהנא says the agent must really be sick, and the גמרא fits this with a ברייתא about 'הולך' and 'את הולך'. אביי and רבא explain why a different משנה does not let agents appoint others, and their answers differ about a gift document. Finally, ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue about what the case of the item teaches, and the גמרא begins to describe where the גט may be invalid.

steps.title: In a Jewish court, a final death verdict means execution
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף finishes his statement. The משנה's rule that a condemned man is still considered alive applies only to a gentile court. In a Jewish court, once the death verdict is issued, he is executed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in a Jewish court, once the verdict for execution has come out against him, they execute him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף finishes his statement. A man sentenced by a Jewish court is as good as dead, unlike someone sentenced by a gentile court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a man led out to execution keeps his חזקת חיים. רב יוסף says that is only because a gentile court might change its mind or be bribed. A Jewish court's final verdict is carried out, so the man is presumed executed.

keyTerms.meaning: The verdict came out against him

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the second half of רב יוסף's statement, which began just before this section. The first half was 'this was only taught about a gentile court.'

phrases.english: But in a Jewish court,
once the verdict has come out against him for execution
they execute him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יוסף's limitation of the משנה's חזקת חיים rule, which began just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After a Jewish court's final death verdict, the condemned man is presumed executed and loses his חזקת חיים.

steps.title: אביי: a Jewish court might still acquit him
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects. Even a Jewish court might find a reason to acquit, so why assume the man was killed?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: In a Jewish court too, it is possible that they will find a merit for him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף. A Jewish court could still find grounds to acquit the man, so he might not be executed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's rule depends on the execution being certain. אביי attacks that certainty. A Jewish court is always looking for זכות for the accused, so it may reopen the case.

keyTerms.meaning: A merit, a reason to acquit

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
A Jewish court too,
it is possible that they will see a merit for him!
phrases.notes: Literally 'they will see merit for him,' meaning they will find a reason to let him go.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind רב יוסף's rule in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that a Jewish court's death verdict is surely carried out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Jewish court can still find זכות and acquit, so execution is not certain and the man should keep his חזקת חיים.

steps.title: Acquittals happen before the verdict, not after
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that a court finds merit before the verdict is final. Once the verdict is final, it does not usually find new merit.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they find merit for him, it is before the verdict is finalized. After the verdict is finalized, they no longer find merit for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his rule. The search for an acquittal belongs to the time before the verdict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף agrees that a Jewish court looks for זכות. He limits that search to the deliberation stage. Once גמר דין has happened, a reversal is rare, so we can still presume the man was executed.

phrases.english: When they see a merit for him,
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't name the speaker, but this is רב יוסף answering אביי.

phrases.english: it is before the verdict is finalized;
after the verdict is finalized
they no longer see a merit for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי חָזוּ לֵיהּ זְכוּתָא – מִקַּמֵּי דְּלִיגְמַר דִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes time periods: before the verdict versus after the verdict.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A Jewish court might acquit at any point, even after sentencing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Finding זכות happens before גמר דין. After the final verdict, acquittal is not expected, so the man is presumed executed.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף: after גמר דין in a Jewish court, we do not expect an acquittal. That is why the condemned man loses his חזקת חיים.

steps.title: Proposed support: a runaway convict is executed on testimony
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a משנה supports רב יוסף. If witnesses testify that a man's verdict was finalized in a certain court, he is executed, with no worry that the court might have acquitted him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him? Wherever two witnesses stand up and say, 'We testify that so-and-so's verdict was finalized in the court of so-and-so, and so-and-so and so-and-so were his witnesses,' this man is executed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to bring a proof for רב יוסף from a משנה about a convict who escaped after sentencing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the verdict is proven, the משנה says to kill him, with no new trial. That seems to show that after גמר דין we don't worry about a later acquittal, which is exactly רב יוסף's point.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רב יוסף. The quote that follows is a משנה in מכות 7a.

phrases.english: Any place where two stand up and say:
'We testify about so-and-so

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנִּגְמַר דִּינוֹ בְּבֵית דִּינוֹ שֶׁל פְּלוֹנִי,
phrases.english: that his verdict was finalized in the court of so-and-so,
and so-and-so and so-and-so were his witnesses'
this man is to be killed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב יוסף, the גמרא looks for outside support.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's rule that after גמר דין we don't worry about acquittal.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מכות: a convict whose verdict is proven by witnesses is executed without a retrial.

steps.title: A runaway is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Maybe someone who fled the court is different, and that tells us nothing about an ordinary convict.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps one who flees is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The משנה is about a convict who ran away, and he may get no second chance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's case is a בורח. Because he escaped, the court will not reconsider his case. That says nothing about a normal convict still in the court's hands, who might still be acquitted.

phrases.english: Perhaps one who flees is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. רב יוסף's rule itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's case involves a runaway, which may be an exception and not represent ordinary convicts.

steps.title: Second proof attempt: death reports from a Jewish court versus gentile officials
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. If a Jewish court says a man died or was killed, his wife may remarry. If gentile court officials say it, she may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If one heard from a Jewish court that they were saying 'So-and-so died' or 'So-and-so was killed,' they let his wife remarry. If he heard it from gentile court officials, 'So-and-so died' or 'So-and-so was killed,' they do not let his wife remarry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new attempt to support רב יוסף from a ברייתא about death reports. The analysis of this source continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats a Jewish court's report as reliable enough to free a wife, but not a gentile official's report. The גמרא will try to read 'was killed' as 'was sentenced to death,' which would back רב יוסף. Steps 7-9 test that reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, introducing a source as proof

steps.confusionAlert: This step only quotes the source. The גמרא draws out the proof in Steps 7-8 and then pushes it off in Step 9.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִבֵּית דִּין שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹמְרִים
phrases.english: If one heard from a Jewish court that they were saying:
'So-and-so died' or 'So-and-so was killed,'
they allow his wife to marry.
If he heard it from gentile court officials:
phrases.notes: These are the clerks of a gentile court who wrote down who was sentenced or executed.

phrases.english: 'So-and-so died' or 'So-and-so was killed,'
they do not allow his wife to marry.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שְׁמַע מִבֵּית דִּין שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected in step 5, the גמרא brings a new source.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's distinction between a Jewish court's verdict and a gentile court's verdict.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: death reports from a Jewish court let the wife remarry, while reports from gentile officials do not.

steps.title: What do 'died' and 'was killed' mean in the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'died' and 'was killed' mean in the ברייתא. It shows that the literal reading, 'actually died', makes the gentile case hard to understand, because a gentile speaking offhandedly is normally believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'died' mean, and what does 'was killed' mean? If you say they mean he really died or was really killed, then in the matching case with gentiles, why can't his wife remarry? We hold that anyone who speaks offhandedly is believed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is clarifying the words of the ברייתא from Step 6 so it can tell whether the ברייתא really proves רב יוסף. This step rules out the simple reading and sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'died' means he literally died, the gentile officials' report should be accepted, because of the rule of מסיח לפי תומו. Since the ברייתא says the wife may NOT remarry in the gentile case, the literal reading seems wrong. That pushes the גמרא toward a different reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The matching case, the parallel to it
A gentile who speaks offhandedly, without intending to testify

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the Jewish court half of the ברייתא. It is the gentile half that makes the literal reading hard.

phrases.english: What is 'died' and what is 'was killed'?
phrases.notes: These are the two words from the ברייתא in Step 6.

phrases.english: If you say 'died' means actually died,
and 'was killed' means actually killed,
then in the matching case with gentiles,
why should they not allow his wife to marry?
Don't we hold
that anyone who speaks offhandedly
is believed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the wording of the ברייתא brought in Step 6 to see whether it proves רב יוסף.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'died' and 'was killed' in the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The literal reading is challenged because of the rule of מסיח לפי תומו. The answer comes in the next step.

steps.title: The words mean 'going out to die', which supports רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'died' means he was taken out to be executed. Since the ברייתא lets his wife remarry when a Jewish court said so, we assume the execution happened, just as רב יוסף said.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, doesn't 'died' mean he was going out to die, and 'was killed' mean he was going out to be killed? And the ברייתא teaches that if it was a Jewish court, his wife may remarry!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes the other reading of the ברייתא and draws the proof for רב יוסף from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא is about a man only being led out to execution, a Jewish court's sentence is enough to let his wife remarry. That means we do not worry that the court found a new reason to acquit him after the final verdict, which is exactly רב יוסף's position from Step 3. The gentile half also fits רב יוסף: a gentile court's sentence does not make the man presumed dead.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it that... (introduces the reading the גמרא is pushing toward)

phrases.english: Rather, isn't 'died' going out to die,
and 'was killed' going out to be killed?
And it teaches: in a Jewish court,
they allow his wife to marry!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having ruled out the literal reading in Step 7, the גמרא adopts the 'going out to die' reading and draws the proof.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's rule that after a final verdict the court does not usually find new merit, so we assume the man was executed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: a Jewish court's report of 'died' or 'was killed', read as 'going out to die', allows the wife to remarry.

steps.title: The words can mean literally died; gentiles lie to back up their verdict
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The ברייתא may mean he literally died. Gentile officials are not believed because the rule of מסיח לפי תומו only applies when the gentile has nothing at stake. Here they want to make their verdict look carried out, so they might lie.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it means he actually died or was actually killed. As for why the matching gentile case doesn't work, given that we hold anyone speaking offhandedly is believed: that is only in a matter that doesn't concern them. In a matter that does concern them, they tend to back up their lies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof for רב יוסף by explaining the gentile case another way, so the literal reading of the ברייתא can stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of מסיח לפי תומו only works when the gentile has no personal interest in what he says. Court officials do have an interest: they want people to think their sentence was carried out. Once that is explained, there is no need to read 'died' as 'going out to die', and the ברייתא no longer proves רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (introduces the answer that keeps the original reading)
It concerns them, they have a stake in it

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not prove רב יוסף, because it can be read as literal death. A gentile who speaks offhandedly is believed only about matters that do not concern him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step sets a limit on מסיח לפי תומו: it does not apply when the gentile has a personal stake in the claim.

phrases.english: Really, it means actually died and actually killed;
and as for why not in the matching case with gentiles,
given that we hold

phrases.aramaic: דְּכֹל מֵסִיחַ לְפִי תּוּמּוֹ הֵימוֹנֵי מְהֵימְנִי –
phrases.english: that anyone who speaks offhandedly is believed:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּמִילְּתָא דְּלָא שָׁיְיכִי בַּהּ,
phrases.english: that applies only to a matter that doesn't concern them,
but in a matter that does concern them,
they tend to back up their lies.
phrases.notes: The officials want people to think their sentence was carried out, even if it wasn't.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 8 by answering the difficulty raised in Step 7 a different way.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא for רב יוסף. It does not disprove רב יוסף himself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the literal reading was impossible. But the gentile case can be explained by their motive to back up their verdict, so the literal reading works.

steps.title: An agent bringing a גט in ארץ ישראל who falls sick
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: an agent bringing a גט in ארץ ישראל who falls sick may send it with another agent. If the husband also asked him to collect an item from the wife, he may not, because the husband does not want his deposit in someone else's hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who brings a גט in ארץ ישראל and becomes sick may send it with someone else. But if the husband told him, 'Take such-and-such item from her for me,' he may not send it with someone else, because the husband doesn't want his deposit in another person's hands.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches when a sick agent may pass a גט on to a second agent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a sick agent may hand the גט to another agent. But if the husband also gave him a job involving the husband's property, the husband clearly chose this person to be trusted with it. So the agent cannot hand the whole job over to someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (start of a new משנה)
An agent bringing a bill of divorce
He sends it with someone else
His deposit, an item left in someone's care

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who brings a גט in ארץ ישראל and became sick,
may send it with another person.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אָמַר לוֹ: ״טוֹל לִי הֵימֶנָּה חֵפֶץ פְּלוֹנִי״ –
phrases.english: But if he said to him: 'Take such-and-such item from her for me,'
phrases.notes: The husband is asking the agent to collect something he left with his wife.

phrases.english: he may not send it with another person,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁיְּהֵא פִּקְדוֹנוֹ בְּיַד אַחֵר.
phrases.english: because he doesn't want his deposit in another person's hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמֵּבִיא גֵּט בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְחָלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: a sick agent passing a גט to another agent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sick agent bringing a גט in ארץ ישראל may pass it to another agent. If the husband also asked him to collect a deposit from the wife, he may not.

steps.title: רב כהנא: The word 'became sick' in the משנה is exact
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא teaches that the משנה's condition 'חלה' is meant precisely. Only a sick שליח may send the גט with another.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב כהנא said: We learned 'he became sick.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the new משנה. רב כהנא points to the word 'חלה' and says it is a real condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a שליח who became sick may send the גט through another שליח. רב כהנא is telling us to read that literally. A healthy שליח may not pass the גט on.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who comments on the משנה here

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Kahana said:
"He became sick" is what we learned.
phrases.notes: He means the word really matters: only an agent who got sick may hand the גט to someone else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה quoted in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שליח may appoint another שליח for the גט only if he became sick.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב כהנא needed to say this, since the משנה already says 'חלה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious, since the משנה explicitly teaches 'he became sick'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא by asking what his statement adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'חלה' is printed right in the משנה. So רב כהנא seems to be repeating what we already know.

phrases.english: This is obvious,
the Mishnah teaches "he became sick"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב כהנא's statement in step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The statement only repeats an explicit word of the משנה, so it seems to add nothing.

steps.title: We might have thought 'sick' was only the usual case
steps.stepSummary: Without רב כהנא, we might think any שליח may pass the גט on. 'Sick' would then just describe the common situation. רב כהנא teaches that sickness is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said the same law applies even if he did not become sick, and the משנה says 'became sick' only because that is the usual way it happens. רב כהנא teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing the mistake רב כהנא is protecting us from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a שליח does his job himself unless something stops him. So a משנה might mention sickness simply because that is the normal reason to pass the job on. רב כהנא rules that it is a real requirement and not just a description.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches us (that it is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב כהנא, 'חלה' in the משנה is a real condition and not just the common case.

phrases.english: You might have said

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא חָלָה,
phrases.english: the same law applies even though he did not become sick,
and the reason it teaches "became sick"
is that it teaches the usual way things happen;
so he teaches us that it is not so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a possible mistaken reading that the statement rules out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Sick' only describes the typical case, so any שליח may pass the גט on.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sickness is a real requirement. A healthy שליח may not appoint another.

steps.title: What case could need sickness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the husband said. If he said 'הולך', even a healthy שליח may pass the גט on. If he said 'את הולך', even a sick one may not. And under רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, even a sick one may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If the husband said to him 'Deliver,' then even if he did not become sick he may also send it! And if he said 'You deliver,' then even if he became sick he may not! And if the משנה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, then even if he became sick he may not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא. It asks which case would make sickness the deciding factor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא lists every possible case, and none of them seems to depend on sickness. In each one, the husband's words or רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view already decide the answer. So רב כהנא's 'only if sick' seems to fit nowhere.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Deliver' (does not say who must do it)
A תנא who holds that a שליח never appoints another

phrases.english: What is the case?
If the husband said to him "Deliver,"

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא חָלָה נָמֵי!
phrases.english: then even if he did not become sick, he may also send it!
And if he said to him "You deliver,"
then even if he became sick, he may not!
And if it follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
then even if he became sick, he may not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that sickness is a requirement, the גמרא asks which case it could apply to.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's rule that sickness is required
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In every possible case, the husband's words or רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view already decide the outcome, so sickness makes no difference.

steps.title: The ברייתא behind the challenge
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that with 'הולך' the שליח may send the גט with another, and with 'את הולך' he may not. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that either way a שליח may not appoint a שליח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'Deliver this גט to my wife': he may send it with another. 'You deliver this גט to my wife': he may not send it with another. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Either way, a שליח may not appoint a שליח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that its challenge in step 14 was based on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes the husband's exact words the deciding factor and never mentions sickness. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל goes further and forbids appointing another שליח in all cases. This is why רב כהנא's sickness condition seems out of place.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught (in a ברייתא)
A שליח may not appoint another שליח

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
"Deliver this bill of divorce to my wife":
this agent may send it with another.
"You, deliver this bill of divorce to my wife":

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יְשַׁלְּחֶנּוּ בְּיַד אַחֵר.
phrases.english: this agent may not send it with another.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Whether this way or that way,
an agent may not appoint an agent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the three cases raised in step 14.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא distinguishing 'הולך' from 'את הולך', with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagreeing

steps.title: Three ways to fit רב כהנא with the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: There are three ways to answer. (1) The משנה is a case of 'הולך', and the ברייתא's permission applies only when the שליח is sick. (2) It is a case of 'את הולך', but sickness is different. (3) It follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but sickness is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is a case of 'Deliver,' and that applies only when he became sick. If you want, say it is 'You deliver,' but one who became sick is different. If you want, say it follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but one who became sick is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its challenge with three different options. Each one makes room for sickness to matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In option 1, the ברייתא's permission for 'הולך' is limited to a sick שליח. In options 2 and 3, the usual ban on appointing another שליח stays in place. Sickness is then a special exception, since the husband would surely agree to it.
steps.whatToRemember: All three answers keep רב כהנא's rule. Sickness either limits the permission of 'הולך' or creates an exception even under 'את הולך' and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.confusionAlert: Answers 2 and 3 do not cancel the rule that a שליח may not appoint another. They keep that rule and treat sickness as a special exception.

phrases.english: If you want, say it is a case of "Deliver,"
and that applies only when he became sick;
phrases.notes: Read the ברייתא's permission for 'Deliver' as covering only an agent who got sick.

phrases.english: and if you want, say it is "You deliver,"
but one who became sick is different;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הִיא,
phrases.english: and if you want, say it follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
but one who became sick is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of steps 14 and 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Three alternative answers: limiting the ברייתא, or treating sickness as an exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every case is already decided by the husband's words or by רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, leaving no role for sickness.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sickness matters. Either it limits the permission of 'הולך', or it creates an exception even under 'את הולך' and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a שליח's sickness is treated as a special situation in which the husband would want the גט passed on.

steps.title: Our משנה seems to contradict another משנה about using a second agent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה, where a sick שליח may send the גט with someone else. It sets this against another משנה, which implies that people told to write and give a גט may not use a שליח.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: a שליח bringing a גט in ארץ ישראל who gets sick may send it with someone else. But another משנה says: if a husband told two people 'give a גט to my wife,' or told three people 'write a גט and give it to my wife,' they should write and give it. That means they themselves may do it, but they may not send a שליח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings our משנה back up in order to challenge it with a different משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lets a שליח hand the job to someone else. The other משנה says that the people the husband spoke to must do the job themselves. So the question is: why may one agent pass the job on, but the other may not?

keyTerms.meaning: And they contradicted it (with another source)
He sends it with someone else

steps.confusionAlert: The other משנה never says outright that a שליח is not allowed. The גמרא reads that from its wording: 'these people should write and give.'

phrases.english: We learned: one who brings a bill of divorce in Eretz Yisrael,

phrases.aramaic: וְחָלָה – הֲרֵי זֶה מְשַׁלְּחוֹ בְּיַד אַחֵר.
phrases.english: and he became sick, he may send it with another person.
And they raised a contradiction: if he said to two people, 'Give a bill of divorce to my wife,'
phrases.notes: This is a different משנה, found later in the מסכת (גיטין 66a).

phrases.english: or to three people, 'Write a bill of divorce and give it to my wife,'
then these people should write it and give it.
They themselves, yes; but an agent, no!
phrases.notes: This line is the גמרא's own reading of that משנה, not part of the משנה itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling how our משנה fits with the ברייתא, the גמרא raises a new contradiction from a different משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה's rule that a sick שליח may send the גט with someone else.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה on 66a implies that people the husband appointed may not appoint a שליח, which contradicts our משנה's allowing one.

steps.title: אביי: The other case is about the husband's embarrassment
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that a שליח is not allowed there because it would embarrass the husband. In our case the husband does not mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: There, what is the reason? It is because of the husband's embarrassment. Here, the husband does not mind.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction by giving a different reason for each case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the other משנה, the husband does not want his divorce spread to more people, so the people he chose may not bring in others. In our משנה, he has already sent the גט out with a שליח, so he does not care if it passes to another person.

phrases.english: Abaye said: There, what is the reason?
Because of the embarrassment of the husband,
here, the husband does not mind.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means our משנה, where the husband already sent the גט out with a שליח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the reason behind each rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות seem to give opposite rules about using a שליח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban in the other משנה comes from the husband's embarrassment, which does not apply in our case.

steps.title: רבא: Spoken instructions cannot be handed over to an agent
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer. In the other משנה the people only have the husband's words, and words cannot be passed to an agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is because they are only words, and words cannot be handed over to an agent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second, different way to answer the same contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the other משנה, the husband only gave spoken instructions, so there is nothing physical to pass along. In our משנה, the שליח holds a real, written גט that he can hand to someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: Cannot be handed over to an agent

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers. אביי says the issue is the husband's embarrassment. רבא says it is that spoken words cannot be passed on, while a written גט can.

phrases.english: Rava said: Because they are mere words,
and words cannot be handed over to an agent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to Step 17's contradiction, different from אביי's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: spoken instructions versus an object that can be handed over
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases look like a שליח passing his job to another.
steps.terutzMaskana: Spoken instructions cannot be passed to an agent, but a written גט can be.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between אביי and רבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in which case the two answers would lead to a different result.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks where the answers of אביי and רבא would actually lead to a different הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons explain the two משניות equally well. So the גמרא looks for a case where one reason applies and the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers given in Steps 18 and 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the reasons of אביי and רבא would give different rulings.

steps.title: The difference is an agent sent to write a gift document
steps.stepSummary: The difference is a שליח told to write a document for a מתנה. This matches the argument between רב and שמואל about whether a מתנה is like a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them in the case of an agent for a gift. It is the same as the argument between רב and שמואל. רב says: a gift is not like a גט. שמואל says: a gift is like a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two reasons give different results for a שליח sent to write a gift document. It links this to the argument between רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under אביי's reason there is no embarrassment in giving a gift, so the שליח may pass the job on. That matches רב: a gift is not like a גט. Under רבא's reason the giver's instructions are still just words, so the שליח may not pass them on. That matches שמואל: a gift is like a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: An agent appointed to write a gift document

steps.whatToRemember: With a gift document, אביי's reason (embarrassment) does not apply, so it matches רב. רבא's reason (words cannot be passed on) still applies, so it matches שמואל.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the reason behind a rule decides how far the rule reaches into new cases.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: an agent for a gift;
phrases.notes: He means someone who was told to write a document giving a gift to another person.

phrases.english: and it is like the dispute of Rav and Shmuel.
Rav says: A gift is not like a bill of divorce.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: מַתָּנָה הֲרֵי הִיא כְּגֵט.
phrases.english: And Shmuel says: A gift is like a bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case of a שליח told to write a gift document. אביי would let him pass the job on, as רב holds, and רבא would not, as שמואל holds.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: a borrower may not lend and a renter may not rent out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a husband who asks the שליח to take an item from his wife. ריש לקיש says this is where רבי taught that a borrower may not lend and a renter may not rent out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if the husband told the שליח, "Take such and such an item from her for me," the שליח may not send someone else. ריש לקיש said: here רבי taught that a borrower is not allowed to lend, and a renter is not allowed to rent out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה, and ריש לקיש explains what rule it teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband wants his item to end up with the person he chose, not with a stranger. ריש לקיש says the same idea applies to anyone holding someone else's item. A borrower or a renter may not pass it on to another person, because the owner never agreed to that.

keyTerms.meaning: Such and such an item; a specific object
A borrower (uses an item for free)
A renter (pays to use an item)
An אמורא, the study partner of רבי יוחנן

phrases.english: And if he said to him
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה. The husband is speaking to the שליח who is bringing the גט.

phrases.english: "Take for me from her such and such an item."
Reish Lakish said:
Here Rabbi taught:
phrases.notes: "רבי" means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who put together the משנה.

phrases.english: A borrower is not allowed to lend,
and a renter is not allowed to rent out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כָּאן שָׁנָה רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה, about the husband asking the שליח to take an item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From our משנה we learn that a borrower may not lend and a renter may not rent out, because the owner wants his item only with the person he chose.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even schoolchildren know that rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rejects ריש לקיש's reading. He says the rule about borrowers and renters is so simple that even young children know it, so the משנה would not need to teach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: Even small schoolchildren know this rule!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן pushes back. He says ריש לקיש's lesson is too obvious to be what the משנה is teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not say the rule about borrowers is wrong. He only says it is too well known for this משנה to be its source. This sets up his own explanation in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Young schoolchildren learning with their teacher
A leading אמורא in ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן agrees that a borrower may not lend. He only disagrees that this is the new lesson of our משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him:

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ, אֲפִילּוּ תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן
phrases.english: This, even schoolchildren
know it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זוֹ, אֲפִילּוּ תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן יוֹדְעִים אוֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects ריש לקיש's claim about what the משנה is teaching.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the borrower/renter rule is the משנה's lesson, not the rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule is too obvious to need a משנה to teach it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: sometimes the גט itself does not work
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives the real lesson. Sometimes the גט is not valid at all, because the שליח broke the husband's instructions. It is like a husband who said to divorce her only in the house, or only with the right hand, and the שליח did it differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the lesson is that sometimes the גט is also not valid. That is because it becomes like a husband who told the שליח, "Divorce her only in the house," and he divorced her in the upstairs room; or "Divorce her only with your right hand," and he divorced her with his left.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives his own explanation of the משנה. Breaking the husband's instructions can make the whole גט invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש saw only a rule about the item: the שליח should not pass it to someone else. רבי יוחנן adds something much bigger. A שליח who does not follow the husband's conditions has not done the job he was given, so in some cases the גט fails, just like in the house/upstairs and right/left examples.

keyTerms.meaning: Divorce her only (in this specific way)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a שליח for a גט must follow the husband's exact instructions. If he does not, it is not just improper; the גט itself can be invalid.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא זִימְנִין דְּגִיטָּא נָמֵי לָא הָוֵי –
phrases.english: Rather, sometimes the גט also is not valid –
because it becomes like one who was told
"Divorce her only in the house,"
and he divorced her in the upstairs room;
"Divorce her only with the right hand,"
and he divorced her with the left.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא זִימְנִין דְּגִיטָּא נָמֵי לָא הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting ריש לקיש's reading, רבי יוחנן offers his own reading of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the שליח breaks the husband's instructions, sometimes the גט itself is invalid, like a שליח who changes the place or the hand the husband named.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש: the משנה teaches that a borrower may not lend. רבי יוחנן: that is obvious; the משנה teaches that sometimes the גט itself fails when the שליח does not follow instructions.

steps.title: A case where everyone agrees the גט is good
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that if the wife came out to the שליח, gave him the item first, and then took the גט from him, everyone agrees the גט is fully valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees: if she went out to meet him, gave him the item, and after that took the גט from him, everyone agrees the גט is a proper גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which case is not part of the argument. If the item was handed over before the גט, the גט is good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the husband got what he asked for before the divorce happened. Since nothing went against his instructions, there is no reason to doubt the גט. This narrows down where the real argument is.

keyTerms.meaning: She went out to meet him

phrases.english: Everyone agrees,
where she went out to meet him
and gave him the item,
and then took the גט from him;
everyone does not disagree
that the גט is a proper גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבי יוחנן's "sometimes" by first giving a case where the גט is clearly valid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the wife gives the item first and then receives the גט, the גט is fully valid according to everyone.

steps.title: Setting up the case where they disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to describe the case where there is an argument: when the husband said something specific to the שליח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they disagree is when he said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to say exactly what the husband said in the case that is argued about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the agreed case is clear, the גמרא turns to the case that is in doubt. The husband's exact words will decide the matter, and they come right after this line.

phrases.english: Where they disagree is when he said to him:
phrases.notes: The husband's words continue on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the agreed case, begins to describe the case that is argued about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is limited to a case defined by what the husband said to the שליח, which the גמרא is about to describe.
